background: In November 2025, Harvard University suffered a data breach later linked to a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion attempt . The data contained 851k unique email addresses relating to the university's alumni and fundraising systems, along with extensive profile information for donors, alumni, parents and some faculty, staff and students.

In Harvard's disclosure notice , the university stated that the breach impacted "personal information such as email addresses, telephone numbers, home and business addresses, event attendance, details of donations to the University, and other biographical information pertaining to University fundraising and alumni engagement activities".
how: The published account does not explain the exact way the data was obtained.
motive: In November 2025, Harvard University suffered a data breach later linked to a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion attempt .
outcome: 850,537 accounts are listed in this breach. This is a count of accounts, not necessarily individual people.

The reported exposed data includes Charitable donations, Citizenship statuses, Dates of birth, Education levels, Email addresses, Employers, Ethnicities, Family members' names, Genders, Job titles, Marital statuses, Names, Occupations, Phone numbers, Physical addresses, Places of birth, Salutations, Social media profiles.

fields.name: Physical addresses
fields.why: Where someone actually lives. Combined with a name this moves the risk off the internet.

fields.name: Phone numbers
fields.why: Enables SIM-swap attacks against SMS two-factor codes, and puts the number on scam-call lists indefinitely.

fields.name: Dates of birth
fields.why: One of the three things call centres ask to verify identity, and it never changes.

fields.name: Employers
fields.why: Connects a personal account to a workplace, which is how attackers pivot from a person to a company.

fields.name: Names
fields.why: Turns an anonymous address into an identified person, which is what makes targeted phishing possible.

fields.name: Email addresses
fields.why: An exposed address may be used in phishing attempts. Treat unexpected messages with caution.

fields.name: Job titles
fields.why: Identifies who has access to what, which is how targets for business email compromise are picked.

fields.name: Charitable donations
fields.why: Adds detail to a profile that can be assembled from several breaches at once.

actions: Move two-factor authentication off SMS and onto an authenticator app, which a SIM swap cannot intercept.
Be sceptical of post and callers who already know your address, knowing it is no longer evidence of anything.
Be alert to phishing. A message may use details from exposed or collected records to appear familiar; verify requests through the service directly.
